report.summary: Read the whole change (paged the parts the diff cut off) with most attention on the new shell-files feature: the Worker getDotfiles/updateDotfiles handlers and their Git writer, the egress read-only credential rule, WorkspaceDO getDotfilesToken and the egress config, the dotfiles.apply op step and tempod Dotfiles, the image changes, the protocol, both clients, the specs and the test reorganisation. Each Artifacts binding call matches worker-runtime.d.ts. The container only gets a read token for upload-pack on the owner's dotfiles remote and none for receive-pack; CI jobs are excluded. A lost D1 write after a push is recovered on the next first save and on the next read. Steps run in the order tab 03 gives and are skipped with the Setup-tab warning. Specs 01/02/03/04/07/09 change in the same PR, and every renamed .cases.ts is still imported by one of the four .test.ts files. Nothing blocking found. I could not run typecheck, lint, tests or cargo: there is no node_modules, and installing or building would write into the read-only worktree, so CI must confirm compilation and the test runs.

findings.text: isDotfilePath accepts a `.git` segment (for example `.git/config`). updateDotfiles would commit it, and tempod's `git checkout --detach --force <sha>` refuses paths with a .git component (verify_path), so every dotfiles.apply after that save fails twice and is skipped. The user always gets the default shell files until they remove the path. Reserve `.git` (any case), or read blobs with cat-file instead of checking out. Not run here: to confirm, build a commit containing `.git/config` and run tempod's checkout command on it.

evidence.why: `.git` matches SEGMENT and is not in DOTFILES_RESERVED, while packages/tempod/src/dotfiles.ts line 158 checks out the whole commit.

findings.text: Every `ng` reply from receive-pack becomes DOTFILES_CHANGED, whatever the reason (for example a server-side object check or a size limit). In that case Reload never helps and the user loops between Reload and Save. Only stale-old-value rejections should map to DOTFILES_CHANGED; other reasons should be ARTIFACTS_API_ERROR.

evidence.why: Reached for any `ok: false` result from parseReportStatus, which returns the raw ng reason without classifying it.

findings.text: The image now installs zsh and makes it the login shell, and tempod never sets SHELL. Agents that prefer zsh when it is present (Claude Code's shell detection may) would then run their commands through the user's .zshrc and Oh My Zsh. Spec 01 only says scripts stay on `bash -lc`. Confirm which shell the agent Bash tool uses in the new image; if it is zsh, set SHELL=/bin/bash for agent processes or update the spec.

evidence.why: This changes the passwd shell, and with zsh now installed, tools that auto-detect a shell may pick it.

findings.text: The egress config (which now carries `dotfiles`) is cached for 60 s. A first save followed within 60 s by a wake whose outbound isolate cached a config without a dotfiles row leaves the fetch without a credential, so dotfiles.apply fails and is skipped with the warning until the next wake. An edge case that recovers on the next wake.

evidence.why: The dotfiles egress grant is only present after the cached config is refreshed.

checked.risk: Real contracts: Artifacts binding (create, get, info, readCommit, readTree, readBlob, createToken, revokeToken), Git smart HTTP receive-pack and pack format, workerd fetch redirect modes, and where the test fake differs from the real service
Real contracts: tempod request dotfiles.apply and the git CLI in the container; Mac TerminalFrame::Ready and TerminalState::size

Failure paths: push rejection and report parsing, readSnapshot when objects are missing, getDotfilesToken failing closed to null, dotfiles.apply skipped with the Setup warning and the warning cleared on success, tempod fetch/checkout errors and deadlines

Idempotency and state: compare-and-swap on head_sha, recovery after a lost D1 write (adoptRemoteTip, first save on the existing tip, ALREADY_EXISTS reuse), the dotfiles.json record and restore, wake order after home.restore

Security: egress read-only rule for the dotfiles remote (HTTPS, same origin, path boundary, upload-pack only, CI excluded), stripping client credentials, manual redirects, token only in the Authorization header, logs going through redactFields, reserved dotfiles- repo names, reserved home paths, no symlink following in place/restore, ownership by ctx.user.id

Build and runtime environment: zsh and Oh My Zsh pinned by commit SHA in versions.json and wrangler.jsonc, root-owned read-only /opt/oh-my-zsh, /etc/tempo/home-defaults copy, home folders chowned, check-versions keeping the default files equal to the protocol constants, D1 migration and snapshot

Tests: every .cases.ts is imported by one of the four .test.ts files; deleted cases are still covered (snapshot image choice in ops.test.ts); retryDelayScale replaces sleeps; dotfiles ops, egress and handler cases exist; CI limits unchanged

The spec: shell and dotfiles behavior, step order and limits, the error code, RPC and egress config, the reserved repo prefix, the UI and Mac changes (terminal tabs, initial prompt, Shell settings) all match the updated spec tabs in the same PR
